name: read_file
description: Read file contents with optional line range. Supports partial reads via start_line/end_line (1-based, inclusive). Always includes line numbers for reference. For large files (>500 lines), prefer partial reads. Examples: read_file { path: 'src/main.rs' } or read_file { path: 'src/main.rs', start_line: 50, end_line: 100 }

path.description: path to the file to read (relative to project root or absolute)

start_line.description: 1-based start line (inclusive). Omit to read from beginning.

end_line.description: 1-based end line (inclusive). Omit to read to end.

name: write_file
description: Write contents to a file. Detects overwrites and reports diff summary (line count change). Supports create_only mode to prevent accidental overwrites. Creates parent directories automatically. Prefer edit for modifying existing files. IMPORTANT: For large files (>150 lines), consider writing a skeleton first and then using edit to add sections incrementally. Example: write_file { path: 'src/config.json', contents: '{...}', create_only: true }

path.description: path to the file to write (relative to project root or absolute)

contents.description: full contents to write to the file

create_only.description: if true, fail when file already exists (prevents accidental overwrites). Default: false.

name: append_file
description: Append contents to the end of a file. Creates the file if it does not exist. Use this for log files, incremental data collection, or adding to configuration files. For modifying existing content in the middle of a file, use Edit instead. Example: append_file { path: 'CHANGELOG.md', contents: '\n## v1.2.0\n...' }

path.description: path to the file to append to (relative to project root or absolute)

contents.description: contents to append to the end of the file

name: delete_file
description: Delete a single file. Use this to remove files that are no longer needed. Does NOT delete directories — use delete_directory for that. This operation cannot be undone. Example: delete_file { path: 'src/deprecated.rs' }

path.description: path to the file to delete (relative to project root or absolute)

name: list_directory
description: List directory contents with file sizes and statistics. Supports recursive listing, depth control, and name filtering. Directories listed first. Skips .git/node_modules/target/dist. Example: list_directory { path: 'src', recursive: true, max_depth: 2, filter: 'test' }

path.description: path to the directory to list (relative to project root or absolute, defaults to project root)

recursive.description: if true, recurse into subdirectories (default: false)

max_depth.description: max recursion depth (default: 1 for non-recursive, 3 for recursive)

filter.description: filter entries by name substring (case-insensitive). Directories still recurse even when filtered out.

name: create_directory
description: Create a new directory, including any necessary parent directories. Use this to organize files into a directory structure. Safe to call even if the directory already exists. Example: create_directory { path: 'src/components/common' }

path.description: path to the directory to create (relative to project root or absolute)

name: delete_directory
description: Delete a directory and ALL its contents recursively. Use with caution — this operation cannot be undone. For removing a single file, use delete_file instead. Example: delete_directory { path: 'src/old_module' }

path.description: path to the directory to delete (relative to project root or absolute)

name: get_symbols
description: Extract symbol definitions from a source file, categorized by type (Types, Functions, Imports, Constants). Supports Rust, TypeScript/JS, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, and more. Supports name filtering. Use this for quick file structure overview before reading in detail. Example: get_symbols { scope: 'src/agent/mod.rs', filter: 'execute' }

scope.description: path to the source file to extract symbols from (relative to project root or absolute)

filter.description: optional: filter symbols by name substring (case-insensitive)

name: search_codebase
description: Semantically search the codebase using the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) index. Returns relevant code chunks ranked by similarity score, with file paths and line numbers. Use this for conceptual searches — finding code by meaning and intent rather than exact text. For exact text matching, use grep instead. The project must be indexed first (reindex_project). Example: search_codebase { query: 'authentication middleware', max_results: 5 }

query.description: the search query describing what to find (natural language, not regex)

max_results.description: maximum number of results to return (default 10, max 20)

name: grep
description: Search file contents with text or regex pattern matching. Returns matching file paths, line numbers, and context lines. Supports regex mode, context lines (like grep -C), and file type filtering. Results capped at 100 matches. Skips .git, node_modules, target, dist, etc. Examples: grep { pattern: 'async fn', context: 3, file_pattern: '*.rs' } or grep { pattern: 'fn\s+\w+\(', regex: true, path: 'src' }

pattern.description: text or regex pattern to search for (case-insensitive by default)

path.description: optional subdirectory to limit search scope (relative to project root). Omit to search entire project.

regex.description: if true, treat pattern as regex (default: false, substring match)

context.description: number of context lines before/after each match (like grep -C). Default: 0.

file_pattern.description: filter files by extension pattern, e.g. '*.rs' or '*.ts,*.tsx'. Comma-separated for multiple.

name: run_terminal_command
description: Execute a shell command in the terminal within the project root directory. Commands have a 30-second timeout and output is truncated at 100KB. Returns stdout, stderr, and exit code. Use this to run builds (cargo build, npm run build), tests (cargo test, npm test), git operations (git status, git diff), or any CLI tool. IMPORTANT: Do NOT run commands that require interactive input, do NOT run destructive commands (rm -rf, force push to main), and prefer non-interactive flags (e.g., --yes for npx). Example: run_terminal_command { command: 'cargo check' }

command.description: the shell command to execute (non-interactive, avoiding destructive operations)

name: run_tests
description: Read-only test runner: detects the project test framework (Cargo.toml -> cargo test, package.json -> npm test, pyproject/pytest.ini -> pytest, go.mod -> go test ./...) and executes it with a 180s timeout, returning exit code, extracted test summary lines, truncated output, and compiler error locations. Use this AFTER editing code to verify the change doesn't break tests — no confirmation needed. Optionally override with a custom `command` or target a subdirectory with `directory`. Example: run_tests { } or run_tests { command: 'cargo test --lib' }

directory.description: directory to run tests in (default: project root)

command.description: custom test command to run (overrides auto-detection)

name: tdd
description: TDD orchestration mode: start/stop/inspect the Red → Green → Refactor state machine for the current session. Call tdd { action: 'start' } to enter TDD mode before writing tests. The phase advances AUTOMATICALLY from run_tests outcomes (a failing suite confirms RED, a passing suite advances GREEN → REFACTOR → DONE), and phase-specific guidance is injected into the context — the agent never needs to track the phase itself. Optional `test_command` overrides the auto-detected command. Example: tdd { action: 'start' }, tdd { action: 'status' }, tdd { action: 'stop' }

action.description: what to do: 'start' (enter TDD mode, restarting any existing session state), 'status' (show current phase), 'stop' (exit TDD mode and show summary)

test_command.description: optional custom test command used for phase gating (default: auto-detected from project)

name: coverage
description: Line-coverage guidance for test writing: runs `cargo llvm-cov` (or reuses the cached report) and lists source files with the most uncovered lines, including concrete line ranges. Call this BEFORE writing tests to target the highest-value gaps, then verify with run_tests and rescan with { action: 'scan', force: true }. Actions: 'scan' (default; runs coverage or reuses cache unless force:true), 'uncovered' (read cached report with path/limit/min_lines filters), 'status' (cache info). Parameters: action, path (substring filter on file paths), limit (max files, default 10), min_lines (minimum uncovered lines per file, default 1), force (rescan even if cache exists). Example: coverage { }, coverage { action: 'uncovered', path: 'hooks', min_lines: 20 }

action.description: what to do: 'scan' (run or reuse cached coverage), 'uncovered' (list gaps from cache), 'status' (show cache info)

path.description: optional substring filter on file paths (e.g. 'hooks' matches hooks.rs)

limit.description: max number of files to list, ordered by uncovered lines desc (default 10)

min_lines.description: only list files with at least this many uncovered lines (default 1)

force.description: force a fresh coverage run even if a cached report exists (default false)

name: a2a_invoke
description: Call a remote A2A (Agent2Agent) agent and wait for its result. Use this to delegate work to other AI agents that expose an A2A endpoint (Agent Card at /.well-known/agent.json). Parameters: url (base URL like http://127.0.0.1:41234 or an /a2a endpoint) OR agent (name of a remote agent configured in Settings → A2A → Remote Agents; the URL is resolved from settings), task (the text of the task to send), mode ('sync' default | 'poll' | 'stream'), skill (optional: skill/agent id to request on the remote side, sent as metadata.skillId — see the remote Agent Card's skills), timeout_secs (max wait, default 120), token (optional bearer token; falls back to local A2A server token). Example: a2a_invoke { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:41234', task: 'Summarize the changes in src/hooks', mode: 'sync' } or a2a_invoke { agent: 'local-orchestrator', task: 'Refactor main.rs', skill: 'code_writer' }

url.description: A2A base URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:41234) or /a2a endpoint; alternative to agent

agent.description: name of a configured remote agent (Settings → A2A → Remote Agents); alternative to url

task.description: the task text to send to the remote agent

skill.description: optional skill/agent id requested on the remote side (metadata.skillId)

token.description: optional bearer token; falls back to local A2A server token

name: run_build
description: Read-only build verifier: detects the project build system (Cargo.toml -> cargo build, package.json -> npm run build, go.mod -> go build ./..., pyproject.toml -> python -m build) and executes it with a 300s timeout, returning exit code, truncated output, and compiler error locations (file:line). Use this AFTER writing/editing code to confirm it compiles — no confirmation needed. Optionally override with a custom `command` or target a subdirectory with `directory`. Example: run_build { } or run_build { command: 'cargo check' }

directory.description: directory to run build in (default: project root)

command.description: custom build command to run (overrides auto-detection)

name: run_terminal_session
description: Execute a command in a PERSISTENT interactive shell session (PTY) that stays alive between calls — `cd`, environment variables, and activated virtualenvs persist. Each `session_id` maps to one shell process (default 'default'); pass `reset: true` to restart it. Completion is detected via a marker with exit code; 30s default timeout (max 300s). Prefer this over run_terminal_command when you need to keep shell state across multiple steps. Example: run_terminal_session { command: 'cd src && pwd' } then run_terminal_session { command: 'pwd' } still shows src.

command.description: the shell command to execute in the persistent session (non-interactive, avoiding destructive operations)

session_id.description: session identifier; commands with the same id share one shell (default: 'default')

reset.description: kill and restart the session shell before running (default: false)

name: glob
description: Find files matching a glob pattern. Returns up to 200 matching file paths. Supports standard glob syntax with ** for recursive directory matching. Automatically skips .git, node_modules, target, dist, and other build directories. Use this BEFORE reading or searching files to discover what files exist. Example: glob { pattern: 'src/**/*.rs' } finds all Rust files, glob { pattern: '**/test_*.py' } finds Python test files.

pattern.description: glob pattern to match file paths. Examples: 'src/**/*.rs' (all Rust files), '*.tsx' (all TSX files), '**/config/*.json' (config JSON files)

path.description: optional base directory to search from (relative to project root). If not provided, uses the project root.

name: edit
description: Perform string replacement in a file — the PREFERRED way to modify existing files. Features: 4-pass matching (exact → line-ending normalized → whitespace-trimmed → Levenshtein fuzzy match), automatic indentation preservation, multi-hunk editing (multiple changes in one call via 'hunks' array), and unified diff preview in results. For new files, use write_file instead.

file_path.description: path to the file to edit (relative to project root or absolute)

old_string.description: the exact text to find and replace. Include enough surrounding context (2-3 lines) to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: the text to replace old_string with

start_line.description: Optional: line number where old_string starts (1-based). Used to disambiguate when old_string matches multiple locations.

end_line.description: Optional: end line boundary (1-based) for range-bounded search with start_line.

replace_all.description: if true, replace ALL occurrences of old_string (default: false, only first match).

hunks.description: Multi-hunk editing: apply multiple replacements in one call. Each element: { old_string, new_string, start_line? }. Use this instead of calling edit multiple times for the same file.

name: todo_write
description: Create and manage a structured task list for tracking your progress on complex multi-step tasks. Break down your work into individual items with unique IDs. Update status as you progress: pending → in_progress → complete (or cancelled). ALWAYS provide the COMPLETE list of todo items each time you call this tool — do not send partial updates. The todo list is displayed to the user in real-time. Use this for any task requiring 3+ distinct steps. Example: todo_write { todos: [{ id: '1', content: 'Read config file', status: 'in_progress' }, { id: '2', content: 'Update settings', status: 'pending' }] }

id.description: unique identifier for this todo item (use short alphanumeric strings like 'a1', 'b2')

content.description: description of what needs to be done (keep under 70 chars)

status.description: current status: valid values are 'pending', 'in_progress', 'complete', or 'cancelled'

name: web_search
description: Search the web for real-time information via DuckDuckGo Lite. Returns up to 5 result titles and snippets (configurable via max_results). Use this when you need information beyond your training data cutoff, need to verify current facts, or need to look up API documentation and version-specific features. Note: This performs a basic web search — for reading the full content of a specific page, use web_fetch with the URL from the search results. The query should be concise and keyword-focused. Example: web_search { query: 'Rust edition 2024 new features', max_results: 3 }

max_results.description: maximum number of results to return (default 5, max 10)

name: web_fetch
description: Fetch and read the full text content of a specific web page. HTML tags are stripped and the result is returned as plain text, truncated at 200KB. Has a 30-second timeout. The URL must start with http:// or https://. Use this to read documentation pages, API references, blog posts, or any online resource in detail. For discovering which pages to read, use web_search first. Example: web_fetch { url: 'https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/' }

url.description: the complete URL to fetch (must start with http:// or https://)

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the user one or more questions when you need clarification, decisions, or input before proceeding. Blocks execution until the user responds. Use this when: (1) requirements are ambiguous, (2) there are multiple valid approaches and you need the user to choose, (3) you need confirmation before a significant action. Each question can include predefined options (with labels and descriptions) for the user to select from. The user's answers will be formatted as Q&A and returned. Limit to 1-4 questions at a time. Example: ask_user_question { questions: [{ header: 'Auth Method', question: 'Which authentication approach should we use?', options: [{ label: 'JWT', description: 'JSON Web Tokens — stateless, good for APIs' }, { label: 'Session', description: 'Server-side sessions — simpler but stateful' }] }] }

header.description: short label for the question (max 12 chars), shown as a chip/tag

question.description: the complete question to ask the user

label.description: concise display text for this option (1-5 words)

description.description: explanation of what choosing this option means or its trade-offs

name: get_diagnostics
description: Get compiler/linter diagnostics for a file. For Rust projects, this runs `cargo check` to find errors and warnings. For other languages, provides guidance on how to run language-specific linters. Use this to understand what's wrong with the code and to verify fixes. Output is truncated to the target file's diagnostics. Example: get_diagnostics { file_path: 'src/main.rs' } returns compilation errors specific to main.rs.

file_path.description: Path to the file to check. Can be absolute or relative to project root.

name: dispatch_agent
description: Dispatch a single sub-agent to handle a specific task. The sub-agent runs autonomously with its own tool set and returns results. Available agents: 'code_writer' (reads/writes/edits code), 'debugger' (debugging & error analysis), 'reviewer' (code review, read-only). Use this for complex subtasks that benefit from focused execution. Example: dispatch_agent { agent_id: 'code_writer', task: 'Add error handling to the login function in src/auth.rs' }

agent_id.description: ID of the agent to dispatch. Options: 'code_writer', 'debugger', 'reviewer'

task.description: Detailed description of the task for the sub-agent to perform

background.description: If true, run the sub-agent in the background (fire-and-forget). The main agent continues immediately and is notified when the background agent completes. Default: false

name: dispatch_agents
description: Dispatch multiple sub-agents in parallel to handle independent tasks simultaneously. Each agent runs autonomously and results are combined. Use this when you have multiple independent tasks (e.g., editing different files, analyzing different modules). Example: dispatch_agents { tasks: [{ agent_id: 'code_writer', task: 'Add tests for auth module', file_path: 'src/auth.rs' }, { agent_id: 'reviewer', task: 'Review the API handlers', file_path: 'src/api.rs' }] }

tasks.description: Array of tasks to dispatch in parallel

agent_id.description: ID of the agent to dispatch

file_path.description: Optional: primary file the agent should focus on

depends_on.description: Optional: IDs of other agents this task depends on. Dependencies run first and their results are injected as context.

background.description: If true, run this sub-agent in the background (fire-and-forget). Default: false

name: memory_search
description: Search cross-session memory (MEMORY.md, daily notes, session history) for relevant past learnings and decisions. Use this to recall what was done in previous sessions.

query.description: Search query - describe what you want to find from past sessions

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

name: git_status
description: Show the working tree status: modified, staged, and untracked files. Use this to see what files have changed before committing.

name: git_diff
description: Show git diff of unstaged or staged changes. Without a file_path, shows a summary (stat) of all changes.

file_path.description: Optional: specific file to diff. If omitted, shows --stat summary of all changes.

staged.description: If true, show staged (cached) changes instead of unstaged. Default: false.

name: git_commit
description: Stage all changes and create a git commit. Use git_status first to review changes before committing.

add_all.description: If true (default), run 'git add -A' before committing. Set to false to commit only already-staged changes.

name: git_log
description: Show recent git commit history. Use this to understand the project's recent changes.

name: git_blame
description: Show who last modified each line of a file (git blame). Use this to find the author of specific code.

name: git_branch
description: List git branches. Shows local branches by default, use all=true to include remote branches.

all.description: If true, show all branches including remote (default: false)

name: git_push
description: Push commits to the remote repository. Use after git_commit to share changes.

force.description: Force push (blocked on main/master for safety). Default: false.

name: git_checkout
description: Switch branches or restore files. Use to navigate between branches or discard uncommitted changes to a file.

create.description: Create the branch before switching (-b flag). Default: false.

file.description: Specific file to restore from HEAD (instead of switching branch)

name: git_stash
description: Save or restore uncommitted changes. Useful for temporarily setting aside work.

action.description: Action: push (save), pop (restore+remove), apply (restore), list, drop, clear. Default: push.

include_untracked.description: Include untracked files in stash (push only). Default: true.

name: generate_diagram
description: Generate a Mermaid diagram from code. Saves the diagram to a temp file (neecoder_diagrams) and returns its path with a preview. Use this to visualize architectures, flows, and relationships. Example: generate_diagram { mermaid: 'graph TD; A-->B', type: 'mermaid' }

name: web_preview
description: Capture a screenshot of a running web page (headless Edge/Chrome) so you can visually verify UI changes (layout, colors, alignment). Start the dev server first via run_terminal_command, then screenshot it. The image is attached to the conversation for review. Example: web_preview { url: 'http://localhost:5173' } or web_preview { url: 'http://localhost:5173', wait_ms: 3000 }

url.description: Full URL of the page to screenshot, e.g. http://localhost:5173

wait_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the page to load before capturing (default: 1500)
